actual_checks: Full literal orientable-filling prompt and all exact source/report/provenance files read; no priors. The substantial contribution identifies why the closest published infinite-family construction misses the orientable hypothesis and proves why its natural upgrade fails, without asserting a universal nonexistence theorem.

FKR Theorem A supplies compact hyperbolic fillings but the introduction explicitly labels their constructions nonorientable. The folding involution would need to reverse boundary orientation to obtain an oriented filling.

For a free orientation-reversing involution on a rational homology 3-sphere, transfer over Q identifies quotient cohomology with invariants: only H0 survives, giving chi=1. The closed odd-dimensional quotient has chi=0, via its orientation cover and multiplicativity. The same argument holds with top degree 2k+1 in the general odd-dimensional statement.

On an orientable boundary, w1 of the filling restricts to zero because the outward-normal line is trivial. Therefore the orientation double cover restricts to two degree-one boundary copies, not the single copy required. No imported Magma computation is rerun or claimed performed.

scope_and_distinctness.exact_scope: Ferrari–Kolpakov–Reid's published infinite families geometrically bound compact hyperbolic four-manifolds, but those constructions have nonorientable fillings. A rational-cohomology proof shows that their free-involution boundary-folding method cannot be made orientable for an odd-dimensional rational homology sphere. The orientation double cover supplies two boundary copies, not the single boundary demanded in the prompt.
